# Explicit String Vacua and the Geometric Selection Conjecture, release 3.3.0

The paper by Deep Bhattacharjee and Ushashi Bhattacharya in its amsart form (56 pages), with its LaTeX source, the arXiv tarball and the checking programs. Contact for this repository: egspl@proton.me (GitHub account creelie).

- New Section 16.5, "Bundles filtered by the line bundles". It treats every Γ-equivariant bundle on X_π filtered by the line bundles of the fixed datum or of the classes 6, 8, 9, 10, with blocks of any size and any extension classes. Lemma 16.20: an extension of L_b by L_a can be reordered when H¹(L_a L_b⁻¹) = 0, so the bundle has every linear extension of the order generated by the nonzero extension groups (Table 12) as a flag order, and a subbundle for every down-set. Theorem 16.21: Y_d = Y_e = 0 for the fixed datum; rank Y_u ≤ 2, or rank Y_d ≤ 2 and rank Y_e ≤ 2, for class 6; rank Y_u ≤ 2 for class 8; Y_u = Y_d = Y_e = 0 for classes 9 and 10. Corollary 16.22: C8_W fails for every bundle on X_π/Γ filtered by the line bundles of the eleven data that has three families.
- The abstract is rewritten to state what is proved.
- The version DOI of release 3.2.0, 10.5281/zenodo.23788190, is recorded.
- `code/filtered_branch.py` (644 checks, output `filtered_branch_results.json`) computes the extension groups and pieces on X_π and recomputes the bounds of Theorem 16.21 for all 120 flag orders and every down-set. The other programs are unchanged (511, 45, 61, 152 checks).
- The Geometric Selection Conjecture is not proved.

Assets: the PDF, the LaTeX source (tex.zip) and the arXiv tarball.
